reference.source: DFC2019 Track3-Truth (HSIP airborne lidar, ANPS about 0.8 m), via the Sat-NeRF EarthVision2022 dataset.zip
reference.heights: WGS84 ellipsoidal (ground median about -17 m; orthometric would be about +12 m here)
reference.acquisition_date: unknown (HSIP U.S. Cities lidar; not stated in the DFC2019/US3D papers)

method.splats: fused export centres placed by model_to_enu then enu_to_ecef, converted to UTM with ellipsoidal heights
method.dsm: max centre height over each splat's footprint disc (1 sigma, capped at 3.0 m), opacity >= 0.5
method.registration: Skyfall-GS/Sat-NeRF dsmr: recursive NCC shift, z offset, no z scaling
method.evaluated_extent: 250 m block (ENU square) inside the truth grid; CLS 65 (unlabelled) and water excluded from all_labelled
method.deviation: Skyfall builds its DSM from rendered depth; this uses splat footprints, so registered MAE is not directly comparable to published numbers

interpretation: Absolute placement: the splat surface sits 1.5 m west, 1.0 m south (1.8 m horizontal, about 5 GSD) and about 1.1 m below the lidar; dsmr resolves shifts on the 0.5 m grid.
That is within the typical no-ground-control accuracy of WorldView-3 RPCs (a few metres CE90); no ground control was used.
MAE of 4-5 m is dominated by the splat DSM itself: centre heights drawn as footprint discs scatter along the needle-shaped splats. A rendered-depth DSM (Skyfall's method) is the next refinement.
The lidar acquisition date is unknown, so scene change since the flight cannot be ruled out; ground and building results agree, which argues against large change.
